title: Why Pay More For Exxon Mobil Stock Than Chevron? - Trefis
content: Today’s big story: Could Nvidia Stock Fall 50%? Follow The Cash Exxon Mobil (XOM) stock costs more for each dollar of profit than any of five oil and gas peers, a group ranging from Chevron to the refiner Valero Energy. Over its latest four quarters, however, Exxon grew sales more slowly than four of those companies and kept a thinner operating margin than three of them. So how much extra are you paying for Exxon, set beside the rival closest to it? Exxon trades at 17.0 times its earnings over the four quarters ended September 30, 2026, compared with 15.8 times for Chevron. Because both are integrated oil and gas companies, Chevron offers a fair comparison. Over those same four quarters, Chevron grew revenue 20.8%, outpacing the 19.5% growth at Exxon. Chevron also turned 14.6% of its sales into operating profit, beating Exxon’s 12.4%. You therefore pay more for each dollar of Exxon’s profit, while Chevron grew faster and kept more of each sales dollar. Every other company in the group costs less per dollar of profit than Exxon. Only ConocoPhillips grew more slowly, at 13.3%, and its stock trades at a cheaper 14.5 times earnings. Because the oil producers and the refiners run different businesses from Exxon, their margins say less about it than Chevron’s margins do. You get one of the world’s biggest fuel businesses. Exxon’s Energy Products segment brought in $290 billion of its $324 billion revenue in fiscal 2025. That segment figure can include sales between Exxon’s own businesses. Management calls Exxon the largest nonstate-owned refiner in the world, running about 3.6 million barrels of crude a day through its refineries. Exxon’s total sales had an uneven year. Exxon’s revenue grew 2.6% from a year earlier in fiscal Q1 2026 and 32.6% in fiscal Q3 2026. The third quarter was also when, management said, conflict in the Middle East constrained supplies of crude, diesel and gasoline, and the lack of supply led to higher market prices. Buyers may be paying extra for something steadier: a long record of rewarding shareholders. On October 30, 2026, management announced a 4% dividend increase, marking its 44th consecutive year of dividend growth. Management plans to keep share repurchases at $20 billion in 2027, assuming reasonable market conditions. The company has also cut $16.9 billion of structural costs since 2019, toward a goal of $20 billion by 2030. The buyback plan was set while fuel was in short supply, and management said on the same call that it expects markets to take well through 2027 to get back closer to normal, possibly longer. So the price appears to assume Exxon can keep its profit and its payouts up once fuel markets settle. Its dividend record shows it has kept raising payouts through earlier downturns, but the four quarters behind today’s price end with a quarter of short supply, so they cannot show that yet. Exxon’s operating margin is the measure to watch in its fourth-quarter report, expected in January 2027. Even the largest company in a group can trail its rivals for a year. That reality remains a good reason to spread your money across many strong businesses rather than lean on just one. The company has raised its annual dividend per share for dozens of consecutive years, a record it says is longer than that of nearly all S&P 500 companies. title: Petrobras Stock After Q3 Earnings - Buy, Sell or Hold for Now? - The Globe and Mail
content: Brazil's state-run energy giant Petroleo Brasileiro S.A., better known as PetrobrasPBR, not only produced more oil and gas but also earned more than a year earlier in the third quarter of 2026. It also raised its annual production and cash-flow forecasts. Those are good reasons to look at the stock, even after its sharp rise this year. There are reasons for caution, too, as profit declined from the second quarter, while spending increased. For investors wondering whether to buy, the question is how much of the expected improvement is already priced in. Petrobras reported revenues of $33 billion, up 40.4% from a year earlier. Profit attributable to shareholders rose 28.4% to $7.7 billion. Excluding one-off items, profit increased 78% to $9.3 billion. Operating cash flow reached $12 billion, up 22%, while free cash flow rose 33.2% to $6.6 billion. Free cash flow measures what remains after investment spending. The stock has already rewarded investors. PBR shares have gained 54.8% in 2026 compared with 41.8% for ExxonMobil HoldingsXOM and 44.3% for ChevronCVX. A large gain alone does not tell us whether a stock is expensive, but it makes the earnings outlook worth examining closely. The results were weaker than the second quarter. Reported shareholder profit fell 25.8%, while profit excluding one-off items declined 15.9%. Lower oil prices hurt earnings, as did higher expenses. Investors should keep that comparison in mind when assessing the much stronger annual numbers. Petrobras produced a record 3.512 million barrels of oil equivalent per day (MMBOE/d) during the quarter. Refineries ran at 99% of capacity, and diesel production reached a record 769,000 barrels daily. Management now expects annual production of 3.3–3.4 MMBOE/d, up from 3.1 million. Offshore platforms are reaching higher output sooner, and the P-79 platform started earlier than planned. Petrobras also raised its operating cash-flow forecast to $45-$50 billion from $35 billion. That forecast uses higher production and revised oil-price assumptions, so the increase does not come entirely from operating improvements. ExxonMobil reported production growth in Guyana and the Permian, excluding Middle East effects, while Chevron increased capacity at existing facilities. For Petrobras, the same basic test applies: does spending lead to more production and enough cash to justify the cost? Fourth-quarter production faces scheduled maintenance and a lower Petrobras share of output under the Búzios production-sharing agreement. Investors should not assume production will rise every quarter. The Zacks Consensus Estimate for Petrobras’ 2026 earnings is $4.95 per share, up 76.8% from $2.80 in 2025. That expected increase gives the share-price rally some support. The forecast still depends on production, costs and oil prices, and it should be treated as an expectation rather than money already earned. PBR trades at a lower forward price-to-earnings ratio than its industry, ExxonMobil and Chevron. Put simply, investors pay less for each dollar of Petrobras’ expected earnings. That makes the stock worth considering after its rally. The discount needs context. Petrobras is state-controlled, which creates a risk that government priorities influence business decisions. A cheaper earnings multiple is attractive only if investors are comfortable with those risks and the earnings used to calculate it. Petrobras raised its annual cash investment forecast to $21-$22 billion from $16.9 billion. Its manageable operating expense forecast increased to $24.2–$25.5 billion from $20.2 billion. Management nevertheless expects those expenses per barrel to fall 2% from 2025. Higher lease payments also use cash. Investors comparing Petrobras with ExxonMobil and Chevron should consider how much remains for shareholders after investment and other commitments. Net debt fell to $57.8 billion. Fitch raised Petrobras’ standalone credit profile to bbb+, although its global rating remained BB. The Amapá discovery may offer future resources, but commercial development is uncertain. The agreement to buy the remaining Logum stake also awaits approvals, and its logistics benefits are expected ahead. PBR looks like a buy for investors willing to accept oil-price swings and the risks of state control. Higher production and expected earnings growth support that view, while the valuation remains below peers despite the rally. Rising spending deserves attention because higher operating cash flow does not automatically mean more money for shareholders. On balance, the price and earnings outlook favor buying over selling or waiting. Petrobras stock is currently a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy). title: ExxonMobil launches $3B debt buyback across four bond series - TradingView
content: ExxonMobil XOM announced on Monday that its wholly owned subsidiaries, Pioneer Natural Resources and Exxon Mobil Corporation, had launched cash tender offers to repurchase up to $3B in outstanding debt. The offers cover four series of notes: Pioneer's 1.9% notes due 2030 and 2.15% notes due 2031, and Exxon's 3.482% notes due 2030 and 4.227% notes due 2040. The $3B repurchase limit applies collectively to all four note series, with purchases prioritized based on the company's acceptance ranking. Pioneer's 2030 and 2031 notes rank first and second, followed by Exxon's 2030 and 2040 notes. The purchases may be prorated if valid tenders exceed the available amount. Accepted notes will be cancelled, and holders will receive the applicable purchase price plus accrued interest. The tender offers are scheduled to expire at 5 p.m. ET on November 20, 2026, with settlement expected on November 24, 2026. title: XOM, CVX, COP: This Analyst Trims Price Targets, Warns Oil Stocks May 'Struggle To Appreciate' - Stocktwits
content: Oil companies are in focus following the midterm elections and the ongoing Iran war, with energy prices fluctuating on anticipation of a deal. Meanwhile, Bernstein revised its price target on three oil majors: ExxonMobil Corp. (XOM), Chevron Corp. (CVX), and Conoco Phillips (COP) following the midterm elections. The analyst lowered the target on all three firms, saying that oil equities may struggle to appreciate. Bernstein lowered the price target on ExxonMobil to $186 from $193 and kept an ‘Outperform’ rating on the shares. The revised target implies an upside of about 9.5% from the stock’s last close. On Chevron, Bernstein cut the price target to $233 from $248 and maintained a ‘Market Perform’ rating on the shares, which suggests an upside of about 7.7%. The analyst downgraded ConocoPhillips to ‘Market Perform’ from ‘Outperform’ and slashed the price target on the company to $122, down from $129. The revised target implies a downside of nearly 13% from its last close. According to The Fly, Bernstein said that it updated its ratings and targets in the oil and gas space following the midterm elections, adding that it believes a de-escalation between the U.S. and Iran is more probable than an escalation. The analyst added that it expects oil prices to normalize. It said that it finds oil companies attractive at oil prices above $75 per barrel, but says oil equities may struggle to appreciate. The analyst also added that it is concerned about profit-taking into year-end or rotation into beaten-down sectors, and noted that it prefers gassy exploration and production companies as a result. Oil prices fell late Thursday after U.S. President Donald Trump said the U.S. does not need a deal with Iran, instead asking Vice President JD Vance to focus "his complete and total attention" on alleged crime and corruption in Democratic-run cities and states. Oil prices declined at the time of writing. Brent crude futures were trading at $95.43 a barrel, down about 0.41%, while WTI crude futures traded 0.47% lower at $88.32 per barrel. With ImmunityBio (IBRX) shares up more than 200% this year, founder Patrick Soon-Shiong has outlined plans to unveil decades of privately funded research at NantWorks over the next 12 months, spanning cancer therapies, AI chips and satellite tech. IBRX stock tumbled 9% on Thursday to $6.07, with shares down 30% for the week and tracking their worst week in nearly two years. Soon-Shiong said on X: “I began the release of our stealth, self-funded programs at Nantworks at a speech at Stanford last night.” NantWorks brings together public and private businesses across healthcare, energy and communications. Soon-Shiong highlighted an antibody search engine he likened to Google, part of an effort to find and treat tumors more precisely. He said that the search engine will use camelid antibodies to make tumors visible on PET scans, then targeting them with radioactive isotopes. The goal is to connect cancer detection with treatment directed at the tumor. He also outlined a system that gives doctors real-time patient data to help them make timely treatment decisions. Soon-Shiong said the tech already had FDA approval, but did not name the product. Meanwhile, Soon-Shiong outlined tech to move data faster as AI systems grow. These include high-speed WiGig wireless tech and optical chips that transmit data using light. He also highlighted U.S. factories to make optical chips and chipsets that connect AI data centers. NantOptiFab is already working in this area, making chips in California that use light to carry information for AI networks, space systems and quantum technology. An SEC filing in August named Soon-Shiong as a director and showed that the company raised $20 million by selling shares to one unnamed investor. His space ambitions include chips for use in space, satellite terminals that communicate using light, and new ways to build and launch satellites. The projects also extend to energy, materials and food safety. Soon-Shiong listed batteries that work in Arctic conditions, non-toxic methods of making graphene, biodegradable alternatives to plastic made from ocean-derived materials, and machine vision to detect harmful substances in food and baby food at the point of purchase. Soon-Shiong also spotlighted a blockchain-based exchange for tokenized securities, or digital versions of stocks and other investments. He pitched it as a way to give companies and investors more control. In January, Nant Global Finance announced plans to bring stock trading, shareholder records and blockchain settlement onto one platform. Its acquisitions included Horizon Globex, which provides technology for the Upstream exchange, and BlockAgent and Equity Stock Transfer, which maintain shareholder records. The company also planned to rename Arkonis Capital, a brokerage and trading platform, NantX. At the time, completing its brokerage acquisitions still required approval from the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA). Soon-Shiong also circled back to ImmunityBio’s work on IL-15, a protein that helps activate the body’s immune defenses. Its drug Anktiva stimulates natural killer cells and T cells, which fight cancer and infections. The company is testing whether it can help patients whose immune-cell counts are too low, a condition called lymphopenia. This also includes a sepsis trial that Soon-Shiong said had been authorized. “Trials will be starting soon in USA and Europe,” he said on Wednesday. The Phase 2 study will test Anktiva in about 50 critically ill adults with sepsis and low immune-cell counts. Researchers will compare the drug plus standard care with standard care alone to see whether it reduces deaths within 28 days. “Longevity at work. Book of our patients’ stories soon,” Soon-Shiong said. The drug is already approved in the U.S. with BCG for certain bladder cancers. ImmunityBio’s approval last month expanded its use to another group of patients whose cancer had not responded to BCG. The update comes shortly after ImmunityBio’s third-quarter results, which showed that net product revenue rose 53% from a year earlier to $48.7 million. For the first nine months, it grew 92% to $143.6 million. The company also said its Quilt-2.005 trial met its main goal in a group of bladder cancer patients who had not previously received BCG. The company is on track to seek expanded FDA approval for these patients in the fourth quarter. Shares of Sellas Life Sciences (SLS) surged 17% in after-hours trading on Thursday after the company said that its key leukemia trial results are expected this month, with its CEO pointing to the treatment’s potential to become a “transformative” immunotherapy if successful. SLS stock fell nearly 5% on Thursday to $8.03, with shares on track to post their third straight weekly decline. The update is related to the Phase 3 Regal trial of Galinpepimut-S (GPS) in acute myeloid leukemia (AML). The November timeline narrows Sellas’ earlier guidance for results in the fourth quarter. “In our ongoing Phase 3 REGAL trial of GPS, we are focused on completing the final analysis following the announcement of 80th event, and we expect to announce topline primary endpoint results this month,” CEO Angelos Stergiou said. “If successful, we believe GPS could be a transformative new immunotherapy for AML patients in second complete remission.” Regal is testing GPS as a maintenance treatment for AML patients who have returned to remission after treatment for a relapse. The study’s main goal is to determine whether GPS helps these patients live longer. GPS is licensed from Memorial Sloan Kettering Cancer Center and targets WT1, a protein found in a range of cancers. Sellas disclosed late last month that the trial had reached its prespecified 80th death, the milestone required to begin its final analysis. This process involves finalizing and reviewing the trial database, revealing treatment assignments and analyzing the results. Beyond GPS, Sellas is advancing its second leukemia drug, Tambiciclib, or SLS009, with investors looking ahead to fresh trial results and a major medical conference presentation. The company has enrolled 40 patients in its planned 80-patient Phase 2 study in newly diagnosed AML, up from 28 disclosed in August. The study includes patients whose disease stops responding early to Azacitidine and Venetoclax, an existing drug combination. Enrollment and treatment are currently continuing, with preliminary results expected in the fourth quarter. The development comes after a completed Phase 2 study in patients whose leukemia returned or failed to respond after prior Venetoclax-based treatment. Sellas will present the findings on Dec.14 at the American Society of Hematology (ASH) meeting in New Orleans. The study enrolled 62 patients and combined SLS009 with azacitidine and venetoclax. Across all doses, 34% of the 59 patients evaluated responded to treatment. At the dose of 30 milligrams twice weekly, 54% of patients with monocytic AML, a leukemia subtype, responded, with median survival of 5.8 months. Among patients with a TP53 mutation, 57% responded, with median survival of 8.8 months. Sellas ended September with $134.7 million in cash and cash equivalents, down from $138.3 million in June. “With $134.7 million in cash and cash equivalents as of September 30, we are well positioned to further advance these programs,” Stergiou said. Third-quarter (Q3) net loss widened to $10.1 million from $6.8 million a year earlier, while loss per share narrowed to $0.05 from $0.06. Meanwhile, research and development spending rose to $7 million from $4.2 million as Sellas prepared for a potential GPS approval application after Regal’s final analysis. Additionally, Sellas is preparing to study SLS009 in pancreatic cancer patients after laboratory findings presented in September. Working with the University of Wisconsin-Madison, researchers tested SLS009 in cancer models grown from patient tissue, including one resistant to Daraxonrasib. They also tested it alongside the experimental drug ZEN3694. Sellas said that the findings support further research into overcoming treatment resistance. However, patient trials are yet to begin. title: Exxon Mobil Earnings Call Highlights Growth and Resilience - The Globe and Mail
content: Exxon Mobil Corp. ((XOM)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call. Exxon Mobil delivered a strongly positive earnings call, highlighting record operating performance, robust cash generation, production growth and a stronger balance sheet. Management also pointed to major shareholder returns, cost savings and project progress, while acknowledging Middle East disruptions, refining uncertainty and execution challenges. ExxonMobil reported $15.4 billion in GAAP earnings and $25.7 billion in operating cash flow for the third quarter. The results underscored the company’s ability to generate substantial cash across its integrated oil, gas, refining and chemicals businesses. The company invested $7 billion in its business and returned $9.4 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases. ExxonMobil also raised its dividend per share by 4%, extending its record of annual increases to 44 consecutive years. ExxonMobil reduced net debt by more than $9 billion during the quarter. Management said net debt relative to capital was the strongest in the industry, apart from possibly one large-cap industrial company. ExxonMobil processes about 3.6 million barrels of crude daily and sells roughly 5.7 million barrels of finished products worldwide. Gulf Coast refineries operated at about 100% crude-unit utilization, while overall utilization was approximately 84%. Diesel yield was about 3.5% higher than in 2019, adding an estimated $1.5 billion to quarterly margins and $3.5 billion year to date. Since 2019, Energy Products earnings per barrel have tripled on a constant-price-and-margin basis, supported by better product mix and lower structural costs. Asset-reconfiguration projects on the U.S. Gulf Coast are expected to increase distillate output by about 100,000 barrels per day. The first phase is underway at Baytown, with further projects planned to improve diesel, lubricant and chemical-feedstock yields at existing sites. ExxonMobil said it has invested more than $200 billion over the past decade. Structural savings since 2019 have reached $16.9 billion, keeping the company on track for $20 billion in cumulative savings by 2030. Excluding Middle East effects, production increased from a year earlier. Continued growth in the Permian Basin and Guyana remained the main drivers of the upstream performance. Production from the Stabroek Block in Guyana has exceeded 1 billion barrels, just 11 years after discovery. ExxonMobil said its fifth development, Uaru, is expected to begin production in the fourth quarter. Cumulative LNG production in Papua New Guinea has surpassed 100 million tons, while the Papua LNG project is positioned for further growth after ExxonMobil increased its working interest and assumed operatorship. In Mozambique, an agreement with Eni will raise ExxonMobil’s operated interest in Rovuma LNG to 50%. ExxonMobil received approval for the Rose Carbon Storage Project and began carbon-capture operations for Nucor. The company said its CCS business now has 11 million metric tons per annum under contract across eight customers. ExxonMobil said it has reduced methane intensity by more than 60% since 2016. The company also received Gold Standard recognition from the United Nations’ Oil and Gas Methane Partnership. Three automated drilling rigs are operating in the Permian and are improving safety and performance, according to management. ExxonMobil expects automated units to account for about 25% of its Permian fleet next year and roughly half by 2028. The Permian program has reached its year-end production guidance ahead of schedule. Management said secondary-recovery technologies offer a path toward significantly higher recovery, although the more meaningful benefits are expected beyond 2030. Trading and optimization volumes are now four times their 2019 level. ExxonMobil said its teams secured feedstocks, redirected supplies and moved products to higher-value markets as conditions changed. Golden Pass Train 1 advanced after ExxonMobil took over work from a bankrupt contractor. Train 2 was expected to be substantially complete by December, while mechanical completion for Train 3 was expected in mid-2027. Management highlighted a broad project pipeline that could contribute beyond 2030. Exploration spending has averaged about $1 billion annually over the past five years, with discoveries in Guyana, Angola and Cyprus, while Product Solutions opportunities include diesel, graphite materials and Proxxima systems. Expected annual synergies from the Pioneer acquisition have increased from $2 billion to $4 billion. ExxonMobil also said its Global Projects organization is executing twice as many mega-projects as international oil company peers, at 20% lower cost and 20% faster scheduled time. ExxonMobil continues working with partners and Mozambique’s government toward a final investment decision for Rovuma LNG. Management said combining the upstream and downstream portions could improve capital efficiency, although the potential benefit has not been quantified. The European Parliament voted to delay implementation of the EU Methane Regulation by three years. ExxonMobil said the additional time should help the industry build compliance systems after the required implementation steps are defined. The continuing Middle East conflict has disrupted trade flows and constrained supplies of crude, diesel, gasoline and other products. Those disruptions have contributed to tighter markets and higher prices. ExxonMobil maintained its estimate of a 350,000-barrel-per-day impact in the fourth quarter, concentrated largely in Qatar LNG after facility damage and lost trains. UAE production was near historical levels, but logistics constraints delayed sales and limited the movement of barrels. Management estimated that about one-third of the global product shortage was linked to difficulties moving clean products out of the Middle East. It also estimated that roughly half of Russia’s refining capacity was offline, turning the country from a net exporter into a net importer of clean products. Management said a return to balance depends on the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, an end to attacks on regional refining facilities and repairs to damaged plants. China’s export levels will also matter, and normalization could take well through next year or longer. The bankruptcy of a contractor created difficulties at Golden Pass and required ExxonMobil to take over the work. The company is progressing with remaining contractors and QatarEnergy. ExxonMobil described Venezuela’s resources as difficult to develop because of crude quality and production challenges. Management said fiscal and legal frameworks, along with investor protections, still need major changes before the company would consider committing significant resources. Historical project structures in Kazakhstan have created complexity and limited effective resource development. ExxonMobil is working with partners and the government on a revised proposal, but discussions remain ongoing and could take time. ExxonMobil called the original EU Methane Regulation timetable unworkable because the compliance deadline preceded the rules needed to implement it. The company said it would have stopped importing into Europe without a workable compliance path. ExxonMobil does not plan to hold a formal corporate plan update in December, unlike in recent years. Instead, it expects to reaffirm key 2027 planning metrics in a press release and provide more detail with fourth-quarter results. ExxonMobil expects Uaru to start in the fourth quarter, Gulf Coast projects to add about 100,000 barrels per day of distillate yield and automated rigs to reach half of the Permian fleet by 2028. The company also targets $20 billion in cumulative savings by 2030 and plans $20 billion of share repurchases in 2027, assuming reasonable market conditions. The company expects Golden Pass Train 2 to be substantially complete by December and Train 3 to reach mechanical completion in mid-2027. Rovuma LNG is still targeted for a final investment decision by year-end, while refining disruptions may persist through next year or longer and the Middle East is expected to reduce fourth-quarter output by 350,000 barrels per day. ExxonMobil’s call presented a company with strong earnings, cash flow and financial flexibility, supported by production growth and disciplined investment. However, Middle East disruptions, refining uncertainty and complex international projects remain important risks for investors to monitor. © Copyright 2026 The Globe and Mail Inc. The project targets a new source of non-associated gas and condensate production, broadening the companys output mix in the basin. The question is how Longtail and its wider offshore build-out will shape the path ahead. ExxonMobil operates a large global portfolio of crude oil and natural gas projects, serving as a major supplier of hydrocarbons to international markets. Its operations span exploration and production, refining, chemicals, and lower-carbon solutions. ExxonMobil develops large, complex projects that require advanced engineering and significant capital. Its scale allows it to pursue developments that smaller companies might not undertake. The integrated model connects production with refining and chemical operations, helping balance results across different parts of the energy value chain. ExxonMobil approved its Longtail development offshore northern South America, adding another large-scale project on the Stabroek block. The company describes Longtail as its largest phase so far in the basin. Final approval marks the shift from planning to execution, allowing contracts, fabrication, and drilling activities to move forward. A commitment of this scale reflects confidence in the underlying resource and the companys ability to deliver complex offshore projects. Longtail adds to a growing series of developments that have made the basin one of the most significant new production areas in the global energy sector industry. Unlike earlier oil-focused projects on the block, Longtail targets non-associated gas and condensate-rich reservoirs. Non-associated gas comes from reservoirs that contain mainly natural gas rather than gas produced alongside oil, while condensate is a light liquid hydrocarbon often found with natural gas. Adding gas and condensate broadens ExxonMobils output from crude into a fuller hydrocarbon mix in the basin, supporting product diversity. Natural gas can serve power generation, industrial use, and export markets. This shift represents a new chapter in the development of the areas resources. The Stabroek block has become known as a prolific offshore area, with a series of large discoveries that have supported multiple development phases. ExxonMobil serves as the lead operator, working with partners to develop the resources. Each new phase builds on infrastructure, experience, and geological knowledge gained from earlier projects, improving efficiency over time. A pipeline of phases allows production to grow steadily as new developments come online. Longtail extends this portfolio, adding gas and condensate alongside existing oil output. The block remains a cornerstone of ExxonMobils upstream growth strategy. Longtail will involve dozens of subsea wells connected to a floating production, storage, and offloading vessel, known as an FPSO. Subsea wells sit on the seabed and send hydrocarbons through flowlines to the vessel, where they are processed, stored, and transferred to tankers. The FPSO for Longtail is sized to handle large volumes of gas and condensate. Floating production systems are well suited to deepwater developments, where fixed platforms would be impractical. Using a proven development approach can help manage execution risk and support timely delivery of the project. The scale of the Longtail commitment reinforces ExxonMobils role as the lead operator in the basin, compared with rivals that have smaller or earlier-stage positions in the region. Leading multiple successive developments builds operational expertise and strengthens relationships with suppliers, partners, and host-country authorities. Large, low-cost offshore resources can provide a competitive advantage in global energy markets. Experience gained across phases can lower costs and shorten timelines for future projects. ExxonMobils position in the basin is one of the most significant growth assets in its global portfolio. Longtail is expected to come online around the end of the decade. Between now and start-up, key milestones include FPSO construction and delivery, drilling of subsea wells, installation of subsea equipment, and commissioning. Market participants will also watch for decisions on gas pipelines that could move volumes from offshore into onshore markets, supporting local power generation and industrial use. Project updates will indicate whether work remains on schedule. Market participants following the company also track  earnings per share and production growth to assess performance across its portfolio. Several specific factors will shape ExxonMobils path from here. Progress on Longtail and other offshore phases will indicate execution on its growth projects. Oil and natural gas prices will influence results across the portfolio. Refining and chemical margins will affect downstream performance. Capital spending discipline will shape cash flow available for owners. Developments in lower-carbon solutions will reflect its energy transition strategy. Production growth from key basins will drive volume trends. The next quarterly update will offer a fresh look at how these factors are progressing.
